title: HelloHQ Sidecar Host-Call Message
description: Tier 1 (Python sidecar) synchronous host calls, carried as newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout. Issued by the plugin mid-dispatch: the plugin writes a request to stdout and blocks on a single stdin readline for the matching response (a 'stop-the-world' RPC the single-threaded sidecar loop makes safe). Each message carries a "type" and a "seq"; a response echoes the request's "seq". These back the ai:inference, plugin:storage, and network:fetch permissions. Lifecycle messages live in lifecycle.schema.json; the top-level dispatch RPC lives in envelope.schema.json.

oneOf.title: ai_complete
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Run an AI completion. Requires ai:inference.

oneOf.title: ai_response
oneOf.description: Host -> plugin. Either a completion result or an error.

tool_use.description: Present when the model invoked a tool instead of returning text.

oneOf.title: storage_get
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Read a key. Requires plugin:storage.

oneOf.title: storage_set
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Write a string value. Requires plugin:storage.

oneOf.title: storage_delete
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Delete a key. Requires plugin:storage.

oneOf.title: storage_response
oneOf.description: Host -> plugin. Reply to storage_get (value | null), storage_set (ok), storage_delete (deleted), or an error.

oneOf.title: http_request
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Outbound HTTP via the host. Requires network:fetch (Verified). The host enforces HTTPS-only, an SSRF guard (no loopback, private or link-local addresses) and the origin allowlist the manifest declares on the network:fetch permission itself: permissions[{"id": "network:fetch"}].scope.origins (bare hostnames or a single-label wildcard; there is no top-level network block). Redirects are not followed. The request body is capped at 8 MiB (error_code request_too_large), and a non-empty body on GET or HEAD is refused (error_code bad_request).

method.description: HTTP method, case-insensitive (the host upper-cases it).

headers.description: Request headers. The host forwards only an allowlist, matched case-insensitively: Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since. Every other header is silently dropped, not rejected. That explicitly includes Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Host, User-Agent, vendor API-key and signature headers (X-API-Key, API-Key, API-Sign, CB-ACCESS-*, OK-ACCESS-*, X-MBX-APIKEY) and any name containing auth, key, secret, sign, token, passphrase, password, session, cookie or cert. Credentials are host-only: a plugin never supplies them. The host logs a per-origin count of dropped headers, never their names or values.

body.description: Request body as text; the host sends its UTF-8 bytes. There is no binary request-body encoding on this transport. Omit it or send "" for a bodyless request (an empty body is treated as no body).

oneOf.title: http_response
oneOf.description: Host -> plugin. Either an upstream HTTP result (status, headers, body, plus body_encoding when the body is not UTF-8 text) or an error (error, error_code). Any upstream status, including 4xx/5xx and an unfollowed 3xx, is a result, not an error.

headers.description: Upstream response headers. Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie2 are always stripped; there is no cookie jar.

body.description: Upstream response body, capped at 8 MiB (over the cap is error_code too_large). When body_encoding is absent or "utf8", this is the body itself: the bytes were valid UTF-8. When body_encoding is "base64", this is the standard padded base64 (RFC 4648 section 4) of the exact response bytes, which were not valid UTF-8 (a PDF, an image, Latin-1 text); decode it to recover them byte-exact.

body_encoding.description: How body is encoded. Absent means "utf8": the host omits the field for text bodies, so the wire is unchanged for plugins written before the field existed, and sends "base64" only for a body that is not valid UTF-8. Readers must treat an absent field as "utf8", must decode "base64", and should fail clearly on any other value rather than guess.

error.description: Human-readable failure text. It never contains the request URL, path, query, headers or a resolved IP address; at most the origin host (for example "Request timed out", "Request failed (HandshakeException)", "Origin \"api.example.com\" is not in the plugin's declared allowed origins"). Do not parse it: branch on error_code.

oneOf.title: propose
oneOf.description: Plugin -> host. Suggest holdings and values for the person to review (docs/plugin/30 section 3). Requires propose:holdings and/or propose:valuations (Verified only, scoped to asset kinds); a plugin that does not hold one gets a permission_denied error. Nothing is written until the person approves each suggestion in the host UI. The plugin proposes against its own source key and never learns an item id, a current value, or an approval decision. The host stamps plugin_id, plugin_version, content_hash, trust_tier, run_id, received_at and host_observed_origins; a batch that carries any host-owned field is refused whole. At most 200 proposals (50 of kind holding) and 256 KiB per call.

oneOf.title: propose_response
oneOf.description: Host -> plugin. One receipt per submitted proposal, in order, or a whole-call error. A receipt carries only its index, an outcome and (for invalid) a reason code; it never carries an item id, a current value, a dedup key or an approval decision, and no plugin-supplied text is ever echoed. Error text is fixed per error_code.

outcome.description: queued: new pending suggestion. duplicate: the same suggestion is already pending. superseded_older: queued, and an older pending suggestion for the same key was superseded. unchanged: equal to the latest value the person already approved. suppressed: the person already declined this exact suggestion, or muted the key. invalid: failed validation; see reason.

reason.description: Present only when outcome is invalid.

error.description: Fixed text per error_code; never contains plugin-supplied text.

error_code.description: rate_limit_exceeded and quota_exceeded are reserved for the persisted limiter (docs/plugin/30 section 3.8) and are not emitted yet. workspace_unavailable: no workspace is open, or not the one the run started in.

reason.description: With bad_request, why the batch was refused.

decimal.description: A canonical-form non-negative decimal string: digits and at most one point, no sign, exponent, leading zeros, or bare '.5' / '5.'. At most 38 significant digits and scale 18 (trailing fractional zeros are not counted). Never a JSON number.

rfc3339_utc.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with an upper-case Z and no offset.

proposal.title: proposal
proposal.description: One suggested holding or valuation. A holding may carry asset_kind, display_name and instrument; a valuation may not (null is tolerated).

source_key.description: Stable key in the plugin's own world (a wallet address, an exchange asset code, a property reference). The host maps it to an item through a binding the person confirms once.

asset_kind.description: Holding only; required for a holding and must be in the permission's scope.kinds.

display_name.description: Holding only; required for a holding. Plain text, no URLs, no control characters, no leading or trailing space.

value.description: Required for a valuation, optional for a holding.

currency.description: ISO 4217, or a crypto code the host knows.

as_of.description: Not later than now + 5 minutes; not earlier than ten years ago.

origin.description: Labelled observed only if the host saw this run fetch it; otherwise the suggestion is shown as 'source not observed'.

reference.description: Plain text shown verbatim; no links.

fetched_at.description: Must fall inside the run window.

reason.description: A closed set of reason codes. None ever contains plugin-supplied text.
